# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

So a user driving the UI through assistive technology could still advance past the provider page and reach "Open Fa" without a provider configured.

This is fine for the ticket's goal (preventing accidental swipe bypass — the gate is a UX guardrail, not a security boundary), and the button-driven path (`_providerDone` → `_next()`) depends on exactly that non-vetoed programmatic navigation. No change required — consider a one-line note in the comment above clarifying that the gate blocks *gesture* scrolling only, so future maintainers don't treat it as a hard boundary.

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,

  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.

          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<details>
<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<details>
<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<details>
<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<details>
<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T06:37:48Z

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<summary>Flow</summary>

  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? ## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

The change is small: adds `physics: gated ? const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics() : null` to PageView. Let me analyze this.

Key consideration: `gated` is `_page == 1 && _providerGateActive`. When gated and the user swipes (blocked), but what if a fling already started? Also, changing physics of a PageView dynamically — Flutter has a known issue: changing `physics` on a scrollable while a scroll is in progress... Actually `Scrollable` handles physics changes via didUpdateWidget and updates `canDrag`... There is a known behavior: `ScrollPhysics` applied via PageView's `physics` changes get applied; but NeverScrollableScrollPhysics blocks `applyPhysicsToUserOffset`? NeverScrollableScrollPhysics has `allowImplicitScrolling`... Actually NeverScrollableScrollPhysics prevents user drags via `shouldAcceptUserOffset` → false. Changing the physics at runtime is fine.

One potential edge: on desktop/web with mouse drag — covered per PR description.

Another potential issue: when the user is on page 1 (index 0) and the provider is not configured, gated is false (gated only when _page == 1), so user can swipe from page 0 to page 1 (that's fine), and from page 1 can't swipe forward (blocked). But can swipe backward from page 1? NeverScrollableScrollPhysics blocks ALL scrolling including backward. Test confirms backward fling stays on provider page. So backward swipe is blocked too. The PR says the step is "button-driven only while the gate is up" — intentional. Hmm, is blocking backward swipe intended? Test explicitly checks it. OK.

Another edge: What about swipe from page 0 when provider not configured — user swipes to page 1, then gate activates. Fine.

Another subtle issue: `_providerDone` calls `_next()` — programmatic page transitions use PageController.animateTo which... does physics affect animateToPage? No — animateTo is driven by a ScrollActivity (DrivenScrollActivity), physics don't veto it. Good.

Now potential concern: NeverScrollableScrollPhysics `applyBoundaryConditions` — NeverScrollableScrollPhysics returns non-zero for boundary conditions, preventing overscroll; fine.

What about `PageController` initialPage — if initialPage > 1 while gate active (e.g., initialPage: 2 in tests with registry)? gated = _page == 1, so false — no block. In real app initialPage is 0. Not an issue in tests with registry? The test `swiping cannot bypass` uses initialPage: 1. If a test pumps initialPage: 2 with registry and no provider configured, user could swipe freely — but the gate is on Continue/skip; last page "Open Fa" — hmm, could a test reach "Open Fa"? In the real app, initialPage defaults to 0, so the user must pass through page 1. But wait — can a user swipe from page 0... no wait, gated only when on page 1. Could the user be on page 0 and fling hard enough to skip page 1 and land on page 2? PageView flings go one page at a time by default (PageScrollPhysics). So no skipping. OK.

Actually wait — there is one subtle issue: `gated` is computed from `_page` in state. While the user swipes from page 0 to page 1, onPageChanged fires when page settles. During the transition... onPageChanged is called when the page changes (after fling completes rounding). At that moment gated becomes true and physics updates. Could a user chain two quick flings: fling to page 1, and immediately fling again before onPageChanged/setState rebuilds? The rebuild happens quickly after page changes. There's a theoretical race but minor. Also, PageView with PageScrollPhysics only moves one page per fling. Between the first fling completing and rebuild, the window is tiny. Not worth blocking; maybe a suggestion? Actually the physics change takes effect on rebuild, which occurs synchronously after onPageChanged... onPageChanged → setState → rebuild in next frame. A fling gesture initiated in that same frame is essentially impossible for a human. Skip.

Another consideration: when gated is true, `physics: const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics()` replaces default PageScrollPhysics — that's fine since no scrolling allowed.

Actually PageView's default physics when null: it uses `_defaultScrollPhysics` = PageScrollPhysics combined with platform physics? Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

<details>
<summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P1[Page 1] -->|Continue / swipe| P2[Page 2 provider]
  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2
  P2 -->|configure provider| P3[Page 3]
  P3 -->|swipe / buttons| P4[Page 4 Open Fa]
```

</details>

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at pub-get/test-build time, so the
      # placeholders must exist BEFORE flutter pub get. Content mirrors the
      # proven build-macos.yml incantation (bare `touch` produced "No file or
      # variants found for asset: .env" on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4).
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored; the tracked placeholder makes it
      # compile (Firebase init is skipped for YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      - name: flutter analyze
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings

  # flutter_app tests sharded ×2 by a deterministic modulo split of the
  # sorted suite (same file list as before — golden + cli_visual stay out,
  # host-locked): each leg is ~half the test phase; pub-cache shared with
  # flutter-analyze so a warm leg pair reuses downloads.
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain

## PR Description

# gh-752: Boarding screens — disable swiping past the provider step

### What changed
Onboarding's `PageView` now uses `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` while the mandatory provider step is gated, so a fling can no longer swipe past "Choose how Fa thinks." and reach "Open Fa" without a provider/model configured. Swiping is restored automatically once a provider is configured.

### Key decisions
- Gate reuses the existing `_providerGateActive` flag (`registry != null && !providerConfigured`), so test-only screens without a registry keep the walkthrough fully swipeable
- `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` instead of a custom physics — it blocks drag, fling, and desktop mouse-drag uniformly; button-driven navigation (`Continue`/`Back` via `PageController`) is unaffected since physics only veto user gestures
- No visual change: physics is not part of the widget tree rendering

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/onboarding_screen_test.dart
```
- New: `swiping cannot bypass the mandatory provider step` (forward and backward flings stay on the provider page)
- New: `swiping is enabled again once the provider is configured`
- Note: `test/golden/onboarding_golden_test.dart` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing Linux font-rendering baseline drift, ~4% pixel diff on all 16 goldens)

  P2 -->|gate up: swipe blocked| P2

The change is small: adds `physics: gated ? const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics() : null` to PageView. Let me analyze this.

Key consideration: `gated` is `_page == 1 && _providerGateActive`. When gated and the user swipes (blocked), but what if a fling already started? Also, changing physics of a PageView dynamically — Flutter has a known issue: changing `physics` on a scrollable while a scroll is in progress... Actually `Scrollable` handles physics changes via didUpdateWidget and updates `canDrag`... There is a known behavior: `ScrollPhysics` applied via PageView's `physics` changes get applied; but NeverScrollableScrollPhysics blocks `applyPhysicsToUserOffset`? NeverScrollableScrollPhysics has `allowImplicitScrolling`... Actually NeverScrollableScrollPhysics prevents user drags via `shouldAcceptUserOffset` → false. Changing the physics at runtime is fine.

One potential edge: on desktop/web with mouse drag — covered per PR description.

Another potential issue: when the user is on page 1 (index 0) and the provider is not configured, gated is false (gated only when _page == 1), so user can swipe from page 0 to page 1 (that's fine), and from page 1 can't swipe forward (blocked). But can swipe backward from page 1? NeverScrollableScrollPhysics blocks ALL scrolling including backward. Test confirms backward fling stays on provider page. So backward swipe is blocked too. The PR says the step is "button-driven only while the gate is up" — intentional. Hmm, is blocking backward swipe intended? Test explicitly checks it. OK.

Another edge: What about swipe from page 0 when provider not configured — user swipes to page 1, then gate activates. Fine.

Another subtle issue: `_providerDone` calls `_next()` — programmatic page transitions use PageController.animateTo which... does physics affect animateToPage? No — animateTo is driven by a ScrollActivity (DrivenScrollActivity), physics don't veto it. Good.

Now potential concern: NeverScrollableScrollPhysics `applyBoundaryConditions` — NeverScrollableScrollPhysics returns non-zero for boundary conditions, preventing overscroll; fine.

What about `PageController` initialPage — if initialPage > 1 while gate active (e.g., initialPage: 2 in tests with registry)? gated = _page == 1, so false — no block. In real app initialPage is 0. Not an issue in tests with registry? The test `swiping cannot bypass` uses initialPage: 1. If a test pumps initialPage: 2 with registry and no provider configured, user could swipe freely — but the gate is on Continue/skip; last page "Open Fa" — hmm, could a test reach "Open Fa"? In the real app, initialPage defaults to 0, so the user must pass through page 1. But wait — can a user swipe from page 0... no wait, gated only when on page 1. Could the user be on page 0 and fling hard enough to skip page 1 and land on page 2? PageView flings go one page at a time by default (PageScrollPhysics). So no skipping. OK.

Actually wait — there is one subtle issue: `gated` is computed from `_page` in state. While the user swipes from page 0 to page 1, onPageChanged fires when page settles. During the transition... onPageChanged is called when the page changes (after fling completes rounding). At that moment gated becomes true and physics updates. Could a user chain two quick flings: fling to page 1, and immediately fling again before onPageChanged/setState rebuilds? The rebuild happens quickly after page changes. There's a theoretical race but minor. Also, PageView with PageScrollPhysics only moves one page per fling. Between the first fling completing and rebuild, the window is tiny. Not worth blocking; maybe a suggestion? Actually the physics change takes effect on rebuild, which occurs synchronously after onPageChanged... onPageChanged → setState → rebuild in next frame. A fling gesture initiated in that same frame is essentially impossible for a human. Skip.
